newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung pledges May elections, Downer says.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung pledges May elections, Downer says.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Sunday that his administration would hold elections next May, Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said.
It was the first time a specific month had been mentioned for polls to return the first elected legislature to replace the Beijing-appointed provisional chamber to be sworn in on Tuesday morning.

After a meeting with Tung, Downer told reporters that he impressed on the new Hong Kong leader the importance of holding the polls within the agreed time limit of 12 months from Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday.
"Mr Tung gave me a guarantee that those elections would take place...and he expected the elections would take place in May of next year," Downer said.
The provisional legislature to be sworn in on Tuesday is to replace a body elected in 1995 under modest democratic reforms introduced by Britain's last governor of Hong Kong, Chris Patten.
